title: Nourishing Japanese Cabbage Pilaf
description: A malty, fluffy Japanese dish featuring savoy cabbage, perfect for meal prep and ovo-vegetarian diets. This recipe showcases the simplicity and flavor of Japanese cooking, with minimal ingredients and easy preparation.

ingredients.name: Medium Grain Rice
ingredients.notes: Japanese short-grain rice is preferred for this recipe.

ingredients.name: Vegetable Oil
ingredients.notes: Use a neutral-tasting oil for best results.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Fresh ginger adds depth to this pilaf.

ingredients.name: Soy Sauce
ingredients.notes: Use low-sodium soy sauce for a healthier option.

ingredients.name: Honey
ingredients.notes: Add a touch of sweetness with pure honey.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Adjust to taste, but start with a moderate amount.

ingredients.name: Black Pepper
ingredients.notes: Freshly ground black pepper enhances flavors.

ingredients.name: Green Onions
ingredients.notes: Finely chopped green onions add a pop of color.

instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add ginger and sauté for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add cabbage and cook for 5 minutes, until slightly wilted.
Add rice and stir to combine with cabbage and ginger.
Add soy sauce, honey, salt, and pepper, and stir to coat evenly.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is cooked.
Fluff pilaf with a fork and garnish with green onions and sesame seeds, if using.
Serve hot, or store in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or freeze for up to 2 months.
